hook.text: Nearly every safety feature in your car today was first tested in a Mercedes S-Class.

buildup.text: ABS, airbags, crumple zones, ESP, pre-collision braking—Mercedes pioneered all of them in the S-Class.

discovery.text: Each new generation introduces technology that trickles down to affordable cars within a decade.

twist.text: The S-Class isn't just a luxury car—it's a rolling R&D lab that subsidizes safety for the entire industry.

climax.text: Even competitors admit: if you want to see the future of cars, look at the latest S-Class.

punchline.text: The S-Class invents the tech. Everyone else copies it.

quiz.question: What is the S-Class's role in the auto industry?

details.summary: The Mercedes-Benz S-Class has been the flagship luxury sedan for over 50 years, consistently debuting safety and technology innovations that later trickle down to mainstream vehicles.
details.whyItMatters: The S-Class serves as a rolling laboratory. Features like crumple zones, airbags, ABS, and active suspension all appeared in the S-Class first before becoming standard across the industry.
takeaways: Crumple zones, ABS, and airbags debuted in S-Class models
It has been the benchmark luxury sedan since the 1970s W116
Each generation showcases Mercedes' latest autonomous driving tech

faq.question: Why do so many innovations appear first in the S-Class?
faq.answer: Its high price point and affluent buyers make it the ideal platform to introduce expensive new technology. Once proven and made cheaper at scale, features migrate to more affordable Mercedes and rival models.

faq.question: Is the S-Class still the best luxury car in the world?
faq.answer: It faces strong competition from the BMW 7 Series, Audi A8, and electric rivals like the Mercedes EQS. But its combination of comfort, technology, and prestige keeps it at or near the top of most rankings.
